newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand took a hammering on Thursday, but managed to end off its worst levels as the Reserve Bank offered support at key levels on the upside, dealers said.

The currency sank to its lowest level in seven weeks shortly after the official opening, hitting a morning's low bid of 4.5640 on the dollar -- its worst level since August 22 -- after finishing at 4.5375/5425 overnight.
It ended the day at 4.5515/5565 on the dollar.
Traders said the currency's slide had been driven mainly by offshore dollar demand and continuing importer dollar buying.

The Reserve Bank entered the market in the early morning, providing liquidity at key levels on the upside, but dealers noted that the bank did not have much room to manoeuvre given the state of its reserves which in September were pegged at 10.04 billion rand.

"The 4.55 level level was broken on the upside in the morning, triggering stop losses by offshore banks. The Reserve Bank offered support at the 4.5600 and 4.5650 level and the market then range-traded in a 4.55 to 4.56 band in the afternoon," a senior trader said.
He noted that the market had been driven by offshore players.
Sentiment was nervous but there was a feeling that the 4.56 to 4.57 level was toppish and some dealers said there was potential for strength on Friday.
Against the crosses the rand was last trading at 7.1258/1382 from 7.0977/1078 on Wednesday and was at 0.3355/3361 marks from 0.3364/3369 marks previously.
Long bond yields motored higher in early trade in sympathy with the rand, but managed to recoup intraday losses to end steady near previous closing levels.
At 1422 GMT the benchmark R150 stock was at 15.375 percent from 15.37 percent late on Wednesday after meeting resistance at the 15.455 percent level.
"Bonds initially reacted to the rand, but we then saw strong institutional buying into weakness above 15.40 percent," a bond trader said.
He said the market was caught short in the afternoon and players covered positions, leading bonds to end steady.
"My feeling is that we will tread water for a while, but ultimately we will have to look at the rand," the dealer said.
Positive news that influential U.S. rating agency Standard and Poor's on Thursday affirmed the country's long-term foreign currency credit rating at BB plus had little effect on the bond market.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 74.55 million rand of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying a net 13.96 million rand of bonds on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 3.06 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.35 billion rand on Tuesday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent, while 90-day BAs were also unchanged at between 15.20 and 15.40 percent.
The daily shortage was quoted at 7.749 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.823 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
